response.internal_assessment: Phase 2. Two months. Millfield is on the list. I read that press release four times before my coffee went cold. I have been telling myself for two years that Millfield is too small, too car-dependent, too regional for this to land here in any meaningful way. I was wrong. Or rather, I was buying time without calling it that. 2008 I had $240,000 in floor plan debt and a market that dropped 40% in 90 days. I cut staff, I renegotiated every contract, I held on. COVID I closed the showrooms and sold cars via video call and home delivery before anyone told me to. I adapted fast. Both times the threat was to my cash flow. This is different. This is a threat to the reason people need what I sell. Not how I sell it. Not what I charge. Whether they need a car at all. That is a different category of problem. But I am not dead yet. Service is not going away. Maintenance is not going away. There are 180,000 people in this county and the nearest major metro is 90 minutes. RoboRide is not replacing a pickup truck hauling a horse trailer to a weekend rodeo. I need to get clear on what I am actually defending, separate the business from the identity, and stop conflating the two long enough to think straight. The dinner last month — 'family institution, not an exit strategy' — I meant it. I still mean it. But I said it before I knew Phase 2 was in two months. I cannot walk it back publicly. What I can do is reframe what the institution IS.

chosen_actions.description: Call an all-hands leadership meeting across all four locations within the next 72 hours. Acknowledge the RoboRide announcement directly — do not let rumors and 'business closing' whispers fill the vacuum. Deliver a clear message: Regional Auto Group has navigated every disruption in its history, we are assessing this one with clear eyes, and no decisions about staffing or structure will be made in panic. Frame the threat honestly but not catastrophically. The goal is to stop the bleeding of morale before it starts, not to pretend there is no wound.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: Time: half-day across locations. No direct financial outlay. Reputational capital: moderate spend — I am acknowledging a threat I previously downplayed.
chosen_actions.reasoning: The inbox shows employees are already circulating 'business closing' notices, some possibly rumors. Every hour I say nothing, the narrative writes itself without me. As CEO and as the person who stood in front of these people last month and said 'family institution,' I owe them a direct conversation before they hear it from a podcast or a competitor's sales floor. Silence reads as panic or denial. Neither serves the institution.

chosen_actions.description: Move $75,000 from operating cash into a dedicated contingency reserve account, separate from floor plan and payroll accounts. This is not a withdrawal from the business — it is a structured buffer. If new vehicle sales soften over the next 90 days as buyers wait to see how the robotaxi rollout lands, I want three months of operating expenses accessible without touching credit lines.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: $75,000 from savings. No income impact. Creates a ring-fenced reserve. Reduces accessible savings from $432,756 to approximately $357,756 in operating accounts, but improves psychological and actual runway cushion.
chosen_actions.reasoning: My loss aversion is real and I am not pretending it is not. But channeling it into a concrete stabilization action rather than letting it drive reactive decisions is the right use of that instinct. I have the runway to do this. Building a reserve now, before I need it, means I will not be making inventory or staffing decisions from a fear-of-insolvency position six months from now. I buy myself decision-making clarity.

chosen_actions.description: Initiate a service department audit across all four locations to identify the revenue ceiling of a service-forward model. I want to know: what is the maximum service and maintenance revenue this group can generate if new vehicle sales decline 30%? Can we grow our fleet maintenance contracts with local businesses and municipalities? Can we build a certified EV technician pipeline starting now, before the wave hits, so we are the service infrastructure for the vehicles that DO come to this region — including robotaxi fleet maintenance? Commission the audit internally, present findings in 30 days.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: Internal labor time: approximately 40 hours across service managers. No external consulting fees at this stage. Potential upside: identifying $200,000-$400,000 in untapped annual service revenue.
chosen_actions.reasoning: I am not ready to announce a pivot. I am not ready to say 'we are a mobility services company now.' The dinner last month set a tone I cannot contradict in week two. But I can quietly begin understanding the shape of what the business COULD become if it had to. The service department has always been the margin engine — it is less visible than the lot but it is what pays the bills when new car sales go quiet. I need hard numbers before I make any public or strategic commitments.

chosen_actions.description: Attend Maria Santos's economic resilience town hall and be visible, not as a victim, but as a voice. Regional Auto Group employs over 200 people in this county. I have standing at that table. I want to understand what policy responses are being considered, who else is in the room, and whether there are coalition opportunities with other business owners facing the same disruption. I am also gathering intelligence. What does the city know about the Phase 2 timeline that was not in the press release?
chosen_actions.resources_involved: Time: 2-3 hours. No financial cost. Potential reputational upside: visible community leadership. Potential intelligence value: high.
chosen_actions.reasoning: I have a normalcy bias score of 0.64. I know I am inclined to underestimate severity. Going to this town hall is a deliberate override of that bias — I am forcing myself to sit in a room where people are taking this seriously, and I will listen even when it is uncomfortable. It also positions me to influence whatever policy conversation is forming, rather than reacting to it after the fact.

response.emotional_state: controlled alarm — the kind that sharpens rather than scatters
response.archetype_self_assessment: builder at an inflection point; not yet a rebuilder, not willing to be an exiter, beginning to ask whether the thing worth building is the same thing I have always been building
response.inner_monologue: I will not burn down what Dad started, but I also cannot protect something that does not exist anymore — so I need to find out, fast, what still does.
